themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 3 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week (2300% increase, z-score 8.69), suggesting a coordinated or sudden outbreak of unauthorized signage across Central Harlem requiring immediate investigation into what is being posted and by whom.
evidence: 3 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 8.69 indicates statistically extreme deviation
2300% increase from baseline suggests concentrated event or campaign rather than gradual trend
reporting_angles: Ground canvas of neighborhoods to photograph and catalog what types of postings appeared and where; interview residents and local business owners about visibility and timeline
Contact NYPD and 311 to determine if complaints cluster geographically or by content type; investigate whether this is protest activity, commercial spam, or organized vandalism

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Spike
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints jumped to 6 last week versus a baseline of 0.8 per week (700% increase, z-score 6.33), marking a significant acceleration in open-air or visible drug-related incidents that warrants investigation into location, patterns, and NYPD response.
evidence: 6 drug activity complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.33 indicates severe statistical anomaly
Concurrent with spike in drinking complaints (3 last week vs. 0.2 baseline, +1100%) suggesting possible coordinated or location-based behavior
reporting_angles: Map the 6 complaints to identify if they cluster in specific parks, blocks, or transit nodes; interview beat cops and community residents about visibility and escalation timeline
Cross-reference with recent NYPD crime data and arrest records to assess whether enforcement has changed; interview NYPD precinct leadership about strategy and resources

themes_detail.label: Public Drinking Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Drinking-related complaints surged to 3 last week versus a baseline of 0.2 per week (1100% increase, z-score 6.35), coinciding with drug activity spike and suggesting possible neighborhood disorder cluster requiring urgent field reporting.
evidence: 3 drinking complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Pattern mirrors drug activity spike last week, suggesting possible common geographic or temporal driver (e.g., reduced enforcement, seasonal change, specific venue closure)
reporting_angles: Visit identified complaint locations to observe conditions firsthand and interview local business owners, homeless service providers, and residents about visible disorder trends
Investigate whether any recent policy or enforcement changes (e.g., park closures, police unit redeployment) correlate with timing of spike

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 19 last week versus a baseline of 4.9 per week (290% increase, z-score 6.97), indicating accelerating complaints about pavement, structural hazards, or maintenance—possibly linked to the litter basket spike.
evidence: 19 sidewalk condition complaints last week vs. 4.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.97 signals extreme statistical anomaly
Concurrent with litter basket request spike (5 last week vs. 0.4 baseline, +1233%), suggesting possible underlying sanitation or maintenance infrastructure failure
reporting_angles: Document specific sidewalk hazards (potholes, broken pavement, debris) in high-complaint blocks; cross-reference with DOT/Sanitation response times and backlog data
Interview residents about whether conditions have visibly worsened or whether complaints reflect deferred maintenance accumulation; assess if litter and sidewalk issues are linked

themes_detail.label: Litter Basket Shortage
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests spiked to 5 last week versus a baseline of 0.4 per week (1233% increase, z-score 9.55)—the highest z-score spike in the dataset—suggesting acute sanitation infrastructure gaps or removal of receptacles that require immediate verification.
evidence: 5 litter basket requests last week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 9.55 is the highest spike in entire dataset, indicating extreme rarity and severity
Correlates with sidewalk condition complaints spike, suggesting possible sanitation service degradation or reallocation of resources
reporting_angles: Request from NYC Sanitation the locations of the 5 requests and determine if baskets were recently removed, damaged, or never installed; check budget/staffing changes
Visit identified locations to assess actual litter accumulation and interview residents about whether trash is piling up or if the spike reflects frustration with existing service gaps
